chapter_theme: Sanmarga (சன்மார்க்கம்), the true path, which in Saiva usage is the path of jnana: laid down by Nandi as a guru-path, it removes the five impurities and the bond of soul and fetter, joins the soul to the Lord, melts the unmelting heart and ends birth. Without clarity there is no knowing Siva; the lower paths serve the simple, and sanmarga is becoming Him.
structure_note: Those who conquered death on the path (1477), Nandi's guru-path and its acts of devotion to the guru (1478, 1479), the fourfold refrain on clarity (1480), and a run of definitions of sanmarga (1481 to 1487), most ending in சன்மார்க்கமே.

1477.reading: Those who saw the flame of scripture that is the manifestation of the Siva-tattva, the declared sanmarga, lost their anger, became Siva-yoga siddhas, conquered death and knew the sign.
1477.nuance: சுருதிச் சுடர் (the flame of the shruti) may be the light that scripture reveals or scripture itself as light. Losing anger (சீற்றம் ஒழிந்து) is set beside conquering death, so moral and yogic attainments stand together. குறிப்பு (the sign) is unclear.

1478.reading: Nandi, the sole leader of Saiva greatness, has laid down one guru-path for salvation; he laid it down so that those in the world may join the divine Siva-way, the good path, and be saved.
1478.nuance: நன்மார்க்கம் (the good path) glosses சன்மார்க்கம். The verse makes the true path a teacher's path (குருநெறி), handed down, not found alone.

1479.reading: Seeing, worshipping and contemplating the guru, touching and praising him, wearing his sandals on the head: for those on earth who serve the guru so, sanmarga is what brings them to release.
1479.nuance: The six acts (தெரிசித்தல், பூசித்தல், சிந்தித்தல், பரிசித்தல், கீர்த்தித்தல், பாதுகம் சூடல்) are all directed to the guru as to the Lord. The verse ties the path of knowledge to devotion to the person of the teacher.

1480.reading: Those who do not know clarity do not know Siva, do not even become the soul, cannot become Siva, and do not end their births.
1480.nuance: தெளிவு here is spiritual clarity, settled knowledge of what is real. சீவனும் ஆகார் (they do not become even the soul) is striking: without clarity one does not truly know oneself as soul, let alone as Siva. The four lines climb from knowing Siva to ending birth.

1481.reading: Becoming Him, destroying the five impurities, being freed by a speech that is silence, the bliss in flawless jnana-experience, and coming to be Him oneself: this is sanmarga.
1481.nuance: ஐந்து மலம் (five impurities) is an extended count of the usual three (anava, kanma, maya), adding maya's products and the concealing power. மோனமதாம் மொழி (speech that is silence) is the guru's silent teaching or the knower's silence. Line 4 is corrupt as printed.

1482.reading: For those of sanmarga there are a face and a seat, a place and a deity, a class and a vision; I shall tell those of every path: listen.
1482.nuance: The verse announces items (முகம், பீடம், இடம், தெய்வம், வருக்கம், தரிசனம்) without explaining them; they may be the marks of each path, given in verses not here. Read alone, it is only a preface.

1483.reading: The means of sanmarga is knowledge and the known; the means of the later paths stands for the simple; those who have left the evil path and are flawless in the fourth state become Him: that is sanmarga.
1483.nuance: ஞான ஞேயம் is knowledge and its object (jnana, jneya). பின்மார்க்கம் (the later or lower paths) are chariyai, kiriyai and yoga, said to suit பேதையர், the simple; it is a ranking, not a dismissal. துரியம் is the fourth state beyond waking, dream and sleep.

1484.reading: If the three lower paths come naturally to the rare disciples who reach sanmarga, then the good path itself is seeking with Siva; the scriptures accept it as the path of the word.
1484.nuance: The verse seems to say the lower three are taken up into sanmarga for the ripe disciple, but the conditional (என்றால்) makes the logic hard to fix. சொன்மார்க்கம் may be the path of the word (scripture) or a pun on சன்மார்க்கம்.

1485.reading: Those who have seen, with themselves, the alien bond, the karma that comes, the states that follow, the root prakriti, the entwined knowledge, and difference upon difference, are of sanmarga.
1485.nuance: அன்னிய பாசம் (the bond that is other, alien to the soul), அவத்தை (the soul's states), மூலப் பகுதி (root nature, mula-prakriti) are technical terms. தன்னொடும் கண்டவர் (who saw them along with themselves) suggests knowing the self and its bonds together, as distinct.

1486.reading: Removing pasu and pasam and joining the soul with Pati, making the unmelting heart melt, reaching the rising of the true form that does not bend, and the stillness in which there is no moving: that is sanmarga.
1486.nuance: The three Siddhanta categories appear together: removing the soul's bound state (பசு) and its bonds (பாசம்), and joining it to the Lord (பதி). கசியாத நெஞ்சம் கசிய puts melting love at the centre of the path of knowledge. அசைவு இல்லாமை is stillness.

1487.reading: The path the sanmargis lay down for reaching is sanmarga and nothing else; for those who do not rest in the path called sanmarga, the path is sanmarga as siddha-yoga.
1487.nuance: Every line opens with மார்க்கம் சன்மார்க்க and the sense turns on how the repeated words divide. The last line may mean that siddha-yoga is the sanmarga for those not yet settled in it, or that sanmarga itself is siddha-yoga; the verse leads into the next chapter on yoga.

links.note: Both promise victory over death to those of disciplined practice: the Kural to those who have gained the power of tapas, Tirumular to Siva-yoga siddhas who have put away anger.

Both make clear knowledge of what is the condition of ending birth: the Kural's mind that has examined and known what is real need not think of another birth; Tirumular says those without clarity do not end their births.
2406 says that when the soul's bound nature is removed and its bonds cut, souls cling to their Lord; 1486 calls that removal and joining sanmarga, and adds the melting heart.

source_issues: 1481 line 4 reads தாவை னாயுறலான, which is not good Tamil; it is probably தானவனாய் உறலான (becoming Him oneself).
1482 lists the marks of sanmarga without giving them; the verse may be a fragment or an introduction to lost or displaced verses.
